clue.text: Talk about hidden danger for part of Persia

indicators.note: the word for talk goes around the other piece, so 'about' signals one word wrapping another

parts.note: to talk is to say
a trap is a hidden danger

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of a lurking peril somewhere in ancient Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: SATRAP was a Persian provincial governor; his province is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrapy was a province governed by a satrap in the old Persian empire.

clue.text: Clear base laid out for a vegetable

indicators.note: letters laid out are set down in a new arrangement, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clearing a base and setting it out to grow vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' rearranges CLEAR and BASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabrese is a green sprouting broccoli, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: The comic success is up-to date

parts.note: a comic or joker can be called a wit
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A comedian's latest triumph is bang up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and modern is idiomatically being with it.

clue.text: Found at the window the cross had broken

indicators.note: something broken has its pieces in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross at a window has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CROSS and HAD. The definition is descriptive: the cord is part of a sash window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash window's sliding frames hang on cords running over pulleys, so this cord belongs to the window.

clue.text: Lily is the leading lady in town

definitions.meaning: a bulbous plant of the lily family with white star-shaped flowers
read whimsically: the 'star' of the little town in the Nativity story, the one that guided the Magi

explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the lily family shares its name with the guiding light over the Nativity town, playfully called its leading lady.

clue.text: One animal which is almost unfit to be eaten by another

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: food gone stale is unfit to eat
another animal, here the lion

explanation.surface: An animal too stale for a meal is fed to a second beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by another' suggests one animal inside another, but the pieces are simply set side by side; 'almost' drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, one kind of animal.

clue.text: Left among actor's last words, they help one to get the answer

definitions.text: they help one to get the answer

indicators.note: one piece goes among the letters of another, so this signals putting inside

parts.note: an actor's cues are the last words of the previous speech, telling them when to speak

explanation.surface: Something left in an actor's final lines helps someone reach the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts L inside CUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hints in a puzzle guide a solver towards the solution.

clue.text: Prepares afresh for the press when it is found in the grass

indicators.note: one thing found inside another signals putting the first inside the second

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses of wet ground

explanation.surface: An editor revises copy after finding it lying in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the press' points to editing, the newspaper sense of press.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit is to revise copy again before publication.

clue.text: Thing to eat, some of which must be supplied for an island

indicators.text: some of which must be supplied for
indicators.note: the answer is only part of the island's name; one letter must be added to it to reach the island, so that letter is taken away here

parts.note: Salamis is a Greek island near Athens

explanation.surface: Some food has to be shipped to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SALAMIS less S gives the answer; equally, the answer plus S is the island. Old-style loose cluing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spiced cured sausage, a food.

clue.text: They enable one to count a hundred among bad practices

indicators.note: letters placed among the others signal putting inside

parts.note: abuses are bad or improper practices
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Counting a hundred cases of malpractice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts A and C inside ABUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: These bead frames are used for doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Parson as one who suffers in advance

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in advance
someone who aches is an acher

explanation.surface: A clergyman described as someone who suffers ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order is reversed: the advance prefix leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a clergyman who delivers sermons, so he is one who preaches.

clue.text: She comes from a story about a fool

indicators.note: one word going round another, so this signals wrapping

parts.note: a story can be a lie
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A woman emerges from a tale concerning an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the whole definition: a lass is a girl, a fitting stand-in for the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass, or Scottish girl, is a female, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Drink which puts one into a saucy condition

indicators.note: one piece is put into another

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky
I is the Roman numeral one
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A drink that gets someone cheeky and merry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts the numeral one inside the word for saucy, giving PERIT, sandwiched by A and the conditional.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: The French port is about to take possession although it looks most like chocolate

indicators.note: one piece is about, or around, the other

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: A French port takes over something that resembles chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: BREST is a naval port in Brittany; 'although it looks' is linking padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is a dark brown, so whatever most resembles it is of the deepest brown.

clue.text: Taking ships to capture the Russian retreating before the French

indicators.note: the reversed pieces come before the French article
going backwards, so the words for capture and the Russian are read in reverse

parts.note: to bag is to capture
Ivan is a typical Russian name
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A retreating Russian is captured by French forces as ships sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns BAGIVAN into NAVIGAB; 'before' puts it ahead of LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Water deep and wide enough for vessels to pass is said to be passable by boat.

clue.text: Digested starting with the fish

parts.note: to digest laws is to set them in order; the word for that begins with a fish of the cod family, read whimsically as if made fishy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digested' means set out as a digest or code, and the answer happens to start with COD.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws arranged into a systematic digest have been reduced to a code.

clue.text: Kind of doctor who puts a judge into profit

indicators.note: one piece put into another

parts.note: boot in the old sense means profit or advantage, as in 'to boot'
a ref, short for referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A medic puts a judge into a profitable position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' preserves the old sense of boot as profit; a barefoot doctor is a rural Chinese paramedic.
explanation.definitionFit: A barefoot doctor is a minimally trained health worker in rural China.

clue.text: Am made a fool of, although collected?

parts.note: humorously, someone made an ass of is 'assed'

explanation.surface: I have been made a fool of, though I have gathered a fortune?
explanation.walkthrough: A punning split of the answer into two words; 'although' and the question mark flag the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Things amassed have been gathered up together.

clue.text: Preposition denoting precise position without victories when in opposition

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: at denotes a precise position, as in 'at the door'
gains are winnings or victories

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on prepositions that turns into talk of losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old sense of outside, so the preposition wraps the victories.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed to something is to be against it.

clue.text: In an election we take part in changing things

indicators.note: the piece for we joins in among the other letters
the letters are changing order

parts.note: us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: Voters taking part in an election that changes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the letters of things to HTINGS; 'take part in' slots the word for we inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The hustings are the campaigning and speeches of an election.

clue.text: Soldier who is Oxford subject among rising artists

indicators.note: one piece set among the letters of another
in a down entry, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree

explanation.surface: A soldier studying at Oxford mixes with up-and-coming painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RAS into SAR, natural in a down entry; 'among' sets the Oxford degree inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a military engineer, a soldier who digs saps.

clue.text: Animal with a hole in its heart

definitions.text: Animal with a hole in its heart

parts.words: Animal with a hole in its heart
parts.note: a large deer whose name has a pit, or hole, near its middle

explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue literally: the letters PIT sit near the centre of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the North American elk, a large deer.

clue.text: Piece of land holds the ring in French river

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: an isle is a piece of land in water
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An island in a French river holds a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts O inside ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isole is a river in Brittany, in western France.

clue.text: Speed in sea is changing and this is the main force

indicators.note: one piece goes in another
letters that are changing will not stay in the order printed, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A ship's speed changes in the sea, the principal force at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes EASIS from the sea and is words before the speed unit goes in; 'Speed in sea' looks like a ship's progress but it is mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the principal stress or force placed on something.

clue.text: Surprise by maintaining that weight exists in dust

indicators.note: the pieces go in the other word

parts.note: ash is dust left after burning
a ton is a weight
something that exists is

explanation.surface: It is surprising to claim that a heavy weight lies in the dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by maintaining that' is padding; the container is signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze or surprise greatly.

clue.text: Engage in what may be silent

indicators.note: the answer is what the word could become once rearranged

explanation.surface: Joining up in something that might be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what may be' rearranges SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to engage or sign up, as for military service.

clue.text: If there were more than one such extra it would be dead and cut up

definitions.text: If there were more than one such extra it would be dead and cut up

parts.words: If there were more than one such extra it would be dead and cut up
parts.note: the plural of this extra piece of text is a rearrangement of the words 'dead and'

explanation.walkthrough: The plural, ADDENDA, is an anagram of DEAD AND ('cut up'); the singular is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is an extra section added at the end of a book or document.
